title: Fuel prices: Petrol falls by 1c while diesel drops by more than R1 a litre from Wednesday - thenational.co.za

 Sign In NEWS Fuel prices: Petrol falls by 1c while diesel drops by more than R1 a litre from Wednesday
 FUEL PRICES
 Ashley Lechman 
 03 NOV 2026, 12:37 3 min read Motorists will see a substantial reduction in diesel prices from Wednesday, while petrol falls by just 1 cent a litre. However, paraffin and LPG prices are increasing. Picture: Tumi Pakkies / ANA Studio Motorists will pay slightly less for petrol and substantially less for diesel from Wednesday, November 4, as the latest fuel price adjustments take effect, while illuminating paraffin and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices are set to increase.
 Petrol 93 and 95 will both decrease by 1 cent per litre, while diesel with 0.05% sulphur content will fall by R1.10 per litre and 0.005% sulphur diesel by R1.20 per litre.
 The Minister of Mineral and Petroleum Resources said the adjustments were based on international and local factors, including higher crude oil prices, increased international petroleum product prices and a weaker rand against the United States (US) dollar.
 The reductions in petrol and diesel prices come alongside temporary fuel levy relief announced by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana during the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) on 21 October.
 The general fuel levy will be reduced by R1.50 per litre for petrol and R3 per litre for diesel from November 4. This brings the levy down to R2.79 per litre for petrol and R1.16 per litre for diesel.
 The relief measure was introduced to ease pressure on households and businesses amid rising fuel costs.
 The department said the average Brent crude oil price increased from $101 to $108 a barrel during the period under review. This was attributed to uncertainty linked to the conflict in the Middle East , including recent attacks on Saudi Arabian infrastructure, as well as higher freight and insurance costs associated with ship to ship transfers.
 International prices for petrol, diesel and illuminating paraffin also increased.
 The department said prices for middle distillates were affected by tight global supply, higher seasonal demand ahead of winter in the Northern Hemisphere and the continuing Russia Ukraine conflict.
 These increases came despite efforts by the G7 to improve global diesel supply, the US waiving certain Russia sanctions and Russia lifting export restrictions.
 The higher international product prices added 80.41 cents per litre to the basic fuel price of petrol, 94.22 cents per litre to diesel and 225.23 cents per litre to illuminating paraffin.
 The rand also weakened against the US dollar, depreciating from an average of R16.21 to R16.55 during the period.
 This contributed to increases in the basic fuel price of 36.93 cents per litre for petrol, 49 cents for diesel and 49.26 cents for illuminating paraffin.
 Another factor affecting the fuel price structure is the slate levy, which has increased from 87.66 cents to 135.84 cents per litre.
 The department said the cumulative slate balance for petrol and diesel stood at a negative R15.876 billion at the end of September.
 In line with the self adjusting slate levy mechanism, the increased levy will be included in the petrol and diesel price structures from November 4.
 Despite these upward pressures, the department confirmed the following adjustments for November: 
 • Petrol 93: decrease of 1 cent per litre.
• Petrol 95: decrease of 1 cent per litre.
• Diesel 0.05% sulphur: decrease of 109.82 cents per litre.
• Diesel 0.005% sulphur: decrease of 119.82 cents per litre.
• Wholesale illuminating paraffin: increase of R2.75 per litre.
• Single Maximum National Retail Price for illuminating paraffin: increase of R3.66 per litre.
• LPG: increase of R183 per kilogram, with an increase of R208 per kilogram in the Western Cape.
 The Maximum Refinery Gate Price for LPG imported through the Port of Saldanha Bay will be R17 100.49 per metric ton, while its maximum retail price will be R39.16 per kilogram from November 4.
